raw_response:
I’m keeping the same wheat-maize rotation on all 10.1 mu. That is what my land is used to, and it is the safest way for me to get grain from two seasons. I do not want to gamble on changing crops. Wheat needs more care in winter and spring, but if I leave it hungry the ears will be light, so I will still put enough base fertilizer and then topdress once when it starts growing hard in spring. For maize, the time after wheat harvest is tight, so I will not do heavy tillage. I will sow quickly, use the hybrid seed people around here use, and put fertilizer in two times, not all at once. Water costs money from the well, so I will irrigate wheat about three times if the season is normal, and maize once, maybe twice only if summer rain is poor. I have family labor, but some work off-farm, so I need a plan that is steady and not too fussy. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than lose yield, but I still have to watch cash, so I am not pushing for the highest rate.
